# {{ site.name | default: site.title }}

{{ site.author.bio | default: site.description }}

I work in Oracle AI Foundations under the guidance of [Dan Roth](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~danroth/) and [Sujith Ravi](https://blogs.oracle.com/authors/sujithravi/), advancing agentic and enterprise AI, multimodal models, and media understanding.

I build applied-science teams and lead research, technical direction and architecture through evaluation and product integration. I bring science, engineering and product teams together across agentic systems, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Console AI and DevOps workflows, including on-call assistance, incident investigation and support automation. My applied-science contributions include multimodal understanding, reasoning and evaluation for Oracle Fusion ERP agents, alongside shared knowledge and semantic-layer research in the Oracle AI Database 26ai ecosystem.

Working with business and technical leaders, I help set priorities across product groups and carry science and architecture decisions through to delivery. The goal is to make AI a core part of product workflows, with shared capabilities that can scale across business units.

I lead research and architecture for Shared Knowledge Store (SKS), a common knowledge and context foundation for Oracle AI applications. The work connects enterprise evidence, relationships and semantic context across agentic use cases, including site reliability engineering (SRE), support workflows and multimodal knowledge. Current research on shared ontologies and semantic layers links structured records with document evidence.

My work on Oracle Support and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Console AI connects agent tools, context and memory with support and cloud workflows. Within Oracle AI Data Platform, I lead applied-science and architecture work on agent discovery, routing and tool selection for Agent Hub, alongside AI Registry’s role in governed capability discovery and reuse. Model adaptation and post-training include published multilingual language-model fine-tuning and enterprise ranking-model training. Creative-media research includes text-to-storyboard evaluation, with scene editing and character-aware search as current directions. I also developed a leadership-coaching assistant prototype.

Research directions: agents that use knowledge, memory and tools; multimodal understanding across language, images and video; evaluation of long-horizon tasks, tool use, reasoning, robustness and bias, supported by reproducible evaluation software.
